summary: Erik Zürcher was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1946–1959) and studied under Paul Demiéville, Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, Édouard Chavannes, and Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, later serving as Leiden's Professor of East Asian History (1961–1993).
Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian. He studied at Het Rijnlands Lyceum Oegstgeest (~1965–1971) and Leiden University (~1971–1984), where he later held an academic post around 1993.

Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1941–1947), he served at the University of Pennsylvania as Professor of Indo-Aryan Languages and Literatures (~1950–1989).

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Harvard College and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, later holding posts at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1890), the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896), and the University of Tsukuba (1897).

Ernest John Eitel worked in sinology and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Tübingen (~1856–1860), he held posts with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1904).

Ernest Mackay was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, and served at the Department of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (~1919–1922).

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Saint-Sulpice Seminary and Collège de France, where he studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and Collège de France (1861).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh (~1961–1964). He served as a professor at Brown University (~1964–2007) and took up a post at Rutgers University around 2007.

Ernst Curtius was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the universities of Bonn (~1833–1834) and Göttingen (~1834–1837). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (~1844–1856), the University of Göttingen (~1856–1868), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1868–1896).

Ernst Gombrich worked in history and art history. He studied at the Theresianum and the University of Vienna (~1928–1933), later holding posts at the University of Vienna, the Warburg Institute (~1936–1976), and the University of London (~1956–1976).

Ernst Haas was an Indologist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and at Bonn and Tübingen. He held posts at the British Museum (1866) and at University College London as Professor of Sanskrit (1875).

Ernst Kuhn was an Indologist, linguist, and Central Asian scholar. He studied at Berlin, Heidelberg, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, Leipzig, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (~1875–1877) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1877–1920).
Ernst Leumann was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at the University of Strasbourg from ~1884 to 1919.

Ernst Steinkellner specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna (~1955–1963), later serving as a director at the University of Vienna and the Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Rudolf von Roth (~1847–1850) and served as a professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1873 to 1885.

Ernst Waldschmidt was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel, and at Göttingen, later holding posts at the Göttingen Academy (1936) and Göttingen University (~1936–1965).

Ernst Windisch was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig University under Curtius, Ritschl, Zarncke, and Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg (1872) and Strasbourg (1875), and served at Leipzig University (1871–1918) and the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (~1892–1918).

Erwin Rousselle worked in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Peking University (~1924–1931), Tsinghua University (~1925–1930), Yenching University (~1931–1938), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1935).
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy who earned his PhD from Kyoto University (~1957–1965). He held a post at Carleton College (~1966–1967) and served as professor and director at Hanazono University between ~1968 and ~2009.
